spiritual_reading.full_translation:
At the first arising of any created mind, two opposing principles are present together: openness to wisdom and resistance to wisdom; the turning of the will toward genuine good and its turning toward what destroys good; the reception of spiritual vitality and the choice of spiritual ruin.

If the Divine were the direct producer of both the good impulse and the evil impulse as such, then a person acting from either would carry no guilt, because the act would be traced back to the First Source and not to one’s own appropriated intention. But if evil does not proceed from the Divine and is not willed by the Divine for performance, then to ascribe evils to the Divine is to speak falsity about the Divine, making the very Love and Wisdom that give all good appear to be the cause and commander of what abolishes good and truth in a person.

paragraph_translations.translation: At the first arising of any created mind, two opposing principles are present together: openness to wisdom and resistance to wisdom; the turning of the will toward genuine good and its turning toward what destroys good; the reception of spiritual vitality and the choice of spiritual ruin.
paragraph_translations.connection: OPENS the chapter by stating the primal duality within beginning consciousness.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Two essences” is taken as two primary opposing principles in a created subject; the multiple pairs in the sentence reinforce the same duality.

paragraph_translations.translation: If the Divine were the direct producer of both the good impulse and the evil impulse as such, then a person acting from either would carry no guilt, because the act would be traced back to the First Source and not to one’s own appropriated intention. But if evil does not proceed from the Divine and is not willed by the Divine for performance, then to ascribe evils to the Divine is to speak falsity about the Divine, making the very Love and Wisdom that give all good appear to be the cause and commander of what abolishes good and truth in a person.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS the opening duality into a moral argument about responsibility and blasphemous attribution.
paragraph_translations.notes: The paragraph hinges on agency: if the Divine causes both opposites, guilt collapses; if not, attributing evil to the Divine is a reversal of truth.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent as a single spiritual teaching: it first establishes the simultaneous presence of two opposite tendencies in nascent consciousness, then argues that moral accountability requires that evil not be attributed to the Divine as its originating cause. The voice and logic remain consistent across both paragraphs.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential (substrate) opening: a compact dual-principle teaching stated by functional oppositions (good/evil; life/death) without administrative apparatus. No narrative seam or alien register.
findings.evidence: Text: “two essences… the light and the darkness… good and… evil… life and death.” This teaches by the *quality and effect* of the two principles (illumination vs obscuration; life vs death), not by jurisdictions, ranks, or named authorities. The spiritual reading did not stumble here; it notes the sentence “reinforce[s] the same duality” and that it “OPENS the chapter.” Removing anything would not improve flow because nothing interrupts the statement.

findings.diagnosis: Clean argumentative continuation in the same correspondential/moral-theological mode. It extends the duality into agency and moral responsibility; no intrusion of administrative voice, no list of officials/territories, no fivefold systematizing addendum, and no bridge connective signaling a seam. The main difficulty is only lacunae/damage in the manuscript, not a change of teaching voice.
findings.evidence: Text: “For if God has himself created them… the one who does them has no sin… If they did not come about from him, nor did he command them… you… speak a lie against God.” This is causality and culpability reasoning (how responsibility arises depending on origin/command), matching the reading’s note that it “hinges on agency: if the Divine causes both opposites, guilt collapses.” There is no moment where the reader reports a mismatch; the reading says the chapter remains “Coherent as a single spiritual teaching… voice and logic remain consistent.”

textual_criticism.summary: No textual-critical disruptions detected (0 excisions, 0 annotations). Both extant paragraphs form a coherent correspondential substrate teaching: primal duality (¶1) followed by an agency/attribution argument (¶5). The only issue is fragmentary damage (missing ¶2–¶4 and lacunae inside ¶5), which does not indicate an administrative overlay or seam expansion.
